problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in N:2{n}^{2}-30<2}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Quadratic Equations and Inequalities
examples.problem: List the elements of the set $A = \{x \in \mathbb{Z}: x^2 - 9 \lt 0\}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $x^2 - 9 < 0.$

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-9 & <0 \\ {x}^{2} & <9 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & <\sqrt{9} \\ |x| & <3 \\ -3<x & <3\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the inequality above are $0,\pm1,\pm2.$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{ 0, \pm 1, \pm 2\}.
$$

feedback.problem: Which set is equivalent to $B={n\in Z:2n-11<-4}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $2n-11<-4.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2n-11 & <-4 \\ 2n & <7 \\ n & <\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the inequality above are $3,2,1,0,-1,-2,….$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
B={…,-2,-1,0,1,2,3}.
$$
